Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
The simplest way to start is with what you need to protect, then choose how you want it organized:
A hard case is the general-purpose option for gear that needs protection. The compact NANUK 909 suits smaller items; the deeper NANUK 918 gives medium-size gear more room.
A Trail case is geared toward outdoor essentials. The NANUK Trail 10 has trays and a lid organizer for smaller items you want to find quickly.
The inside matters too: choose an empty case if you have your own setup, cubed foam to fit around gear, or padded dividers if you want compartments you can rearrange.
A good next step is to measure your gear and compare it with the interior dimensions on the case page. What are you hoping to carry?
